answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by giving every identity a lantern score that only grows after a history of verified, useful work, so a new account starts with no trust for high-value trades. A fable of easy riches fails here, because creating a fresh identity resets that score to zero and costs time the attacker cannot shortcut. Like a comet that appears once and burns out fast, a throwaway identity cannot accumulate the slow, checkable reputation needed to move large value, so faking many agents becomes expensive and pointless.
